subject: history_social
passage: In 1939, the self-taught archaeologist Basil Brown, working at the request of the landowner Edith Pretty, uncovered the outline of a 27-meter ship beneath a mound at Sutton Hoo in Suffolk, England. The wood had rotted away, but rows of iron rivets and a stain in the sand preserved the vessel's shape. In the burial chamber at its center lay gold jewelry, silver dishes from the Byzantine Empire, and the remains of an ornate iron helmet. Many scholars believe that the grave belonged to ______ king of East Anglia who died around 624 CE, though no inscription names its occupant.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: "A king of East Anglia who died around 624 CE" is an appositive: a noun phrase that renames "Rædwald" and adds information about him. An appositive that follows a name at the end of a clause is set off with a comma.
explanation.A: Incorrect. A period would leave "A king of East Anglia … names its occupant" as a fragment without a main verb.
explanation.B: Correct. The comma attaches the appositive "a king of East Anglia …" to the name it describes.
explanation.C: Incorrect. A semicolon must have an independent clause on each side, but "a king of East Anglia who died around 624 CE" has no main verb.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Without punctuation, "Rædwald a king of East Anglia" runs the name and its description together.
